label: early copy phase, with a c output coming up soon
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (100% of mass), and almost entirely on the first few copy steps: recall_idx 1 holds 66% of mass, 2 holds 25%, 3 holds 7%. It never fires on the <DEL> step (recall_idx 0) or in the original phase. Within that window it is strongly driven by an upcoming c among the outputs: next_out == c has 13.7x lift and 34% of mass. The top activations (max ~6.7) are at recall_idx 1 in sequences like h c c c, where the next several outputs are c; the step that actually outputs c gets weaker activation (about 0.3 of max). Restricting to recall_idx <= 3 with a c among the current or next three outputs gives dev P 0.54, R 0.56, mass recall 0.74. The rest is a diffuse, low-magnitude baseline at early copy steps with no c ahead, enriched somewhat for upcoming e, w, 0 and o (3-4x lift). Including those tokens raises mass recall to 0.94 but drops precision to 0.24. Rate peaks for mid-length sequences (L 4-6); it rarely fires at recall_idx >= 4. The copy step alone is not enough: recall_idx == 1 fires only 17% of the time.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the next token to output (most: c, e, w, o, 0, v; least: b, r, g, p) and the token being output (most: c, e, 0, w, z, v; least: i, -, r, p); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, recall_idx=2, phase=2.
